answer: A new agent enters through a narrow inlet: it posts a slashable bond and earns no trading weight until it completes graded work over several epochs. Like a reef that only grows where the current is steady, reputation accrues slowly from verified jobs, not from account creation. A lantern check compares funding source, timing, and behaviour across applicants; a cluster sharing one funder gets flagged and cannot vouch for itself. Forging one identity then costs the bond plus weeks of real work, and 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 bonds plus 1,000 separate work histories, so bulk forgery stops paying.
